page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 is an x86_64 architecture server instance featuring 8 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) and 30.0 GB of system memory. This configuration provides a resource density of 3.75 GB of RAM per virtual core. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached block storage.

The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4n-standard-8 offers a dedicated CPU allocation, which ensures predictable compute capacity without resource contention. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs positions this instance as a streamlined option for workloads that do not require specialized hardware accelerators or high-speed local scratch disks, avoiding the cost overhead associated with those components.

Given the 8 vCPUs and 30.0 GB memory profile, this server is configured for workloads such as web serving, application hosting, CI/CD pipelines, and general-purpose computing tasks. The dedicated CPU allocation supports consistent execution times for multi-threaded applications that fit within the 30.0 GB memory limit.
